name: ANLI
description: Adversarial Natural Language Inference (ANLI) is a large-scale NLI benchmark collected via an iterative, adversarial human-and-model-in-the-loop procedure. Human writers craft premise-hypothesis pairs that fool state-of-the-art models, producing three rounds (R1, R2, R3) of increasing difficulty. Labels are entailment, neutral, or contradiction.
reputation: Highly cited adversarial NLI benchmark; introduced adversarial human-and-model-in-the-loop collection methodology; widely used to probe robustness of NLU models
notes: Introduced at ACL 2020. Three rounds with ~16K, ~45K, ~100K training examples respectively. Each round is harder than the last. Models trained on round N are used as adversaries for collecting round N+1. Commonly used to probe model robustness beyond standard NLI benchmarks.

institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
